name: PSLE Singapore Oral Practice Rubric - Strict
subject: English
description: Upload-ready strict PSLE-style Singapore English Oral practice rubric for reading aloud and stimulus-based conversation. Award high marks only when there is clear evidence of accuracy, relevance, elaboration, and confident spoken delivery. This is a structured practice rubric, not an official SEAB marking scheme.

criteria.name: Reading Aloud - Pronunciation
criteria.description: Reading aloud pronunciation: assesses accurate pronunciation of words, clear articulation, and beginning and ending sounds. Score strictly: repeated unclear words, missing word endings, or uncertain audio evidence should reduce the mark.

rubric_levels.description: Pronounces all or nearly all words accurately and clearly, including beginning and ending sounds throughout. Only rare slips are acceptable, and they must not affect meaning.
Pronounces most words clearly, with only a few noticeable errors. Beginning and ending sounds are mostly secure, with no repeated pattern of dropped or unclear sounds.
Pronunciation is generally understandable, but several words, syllables, or word endings are unclear or inaccurate. Repeated pronunciation issues should remain in this band.
Frequent pronunciation errors, unclear articulation, or missing beginning and ending sounds make parts of the reading difficult to understand.
Pronunciation is mostly unclear, heavily incomplete, or supported by very little usable reading evidence.
No reading attempt or no usable audio/transcript evidence.

criteria.name: Reading Aloud - Expression
criteria.description: Reading aloud expression: assesses pitch, tone, phrasing, and awareness of meaning, purpose, audience, and context. Score strictly: flat, mechanical, or poorly phrased reading should not receive high marks even if the words are mostly correct.

rubric_levels.description: Reads with consistently suitable expression, tone, phrasing, and awareness of meaning throughout the passage.
Uses appropriate tone and phrasing most of the time, but there are noticeable flat, rushed, or unnatural parts.
Shows limited expression. Tone or phrasing is uneven, and meaning is only partly conveyed.
Reads with little variation in pitch or tone. Expression is mostly flat, mechanical, or disconnected from the passage meaning.
Expression is very limited, largely absent, or there is too little usable reading evidence.
No reading attempt or no usable audio/transcript evidence.

criteria.name: Reading Aloud - Delivery and Fluency
criteria.description: Reading aloud delivery and fluency: assesses smoothness, pace, pauses, hesitation, and continuity while reading the passage. Score strictly: repeated pauses, restarts, uneven pace, or choppy delivery should reduce the mark.

rubric_levels.description: Reads smoothly throughout with suitable pace, natural pauses, and very little hesitation or self-correction.
Reads mostly smoothly with appropriate pace and pauses, though there are some noticeable hesitations or small disruptions.
Reading is understandable, but pace, pauses, restarts, or hesitation are uneven enough to affect fluency.
Reading is slow, jerky, or frequently interrupted by awkward pauses, restarts, and hesitation.
Reading is very halting, incomplete, or supported by too little usable reading evidence.
No reading attempt or no usable audio/transcript evidence.

criteria.name: Stimulus Response Relevance
criteria.description: Stimulus-based conversation: assesses whether the student answers the question directly, refers accurately to the picture stimulus, and gives a relevant personal or thoughtful response. Score strictly: generic answers, weak links to the stimulus, or answers that only repeat the question should not receive high marks.

rubric_levels.description: Answers the question directly with accurate, specific reference to the picture and a clear personal or thoughtful response. The answer must show the student understood both the question and the stimulus.
Mostly answers the question and makes a relevant reference to the picture, but details may be somewhat general or not fully precise.
Partly answers the question, but the picture reference is weak, vague, inaccurate, or not clearly connected to the student's point.
Response is mostly generic, very brief, or only loosely related to the picture or question.
No meaningful answer, or the answer is unrelated to the question and picture.

criteria.name: Idea Development
criteria.description: Stimulus-based conversation: assesses elaboration, reasons, examples, explanation, and ability to extend beyond a short or surface-level answer. Score strictly: one-sentence answers, repeated ideas, or unsupported opinions should stay in the lower bands.

rubric_levels.description: Develops ideas clearly with relevant reasons, examples, explanation, and thoughtful extension. The response should move beyond one simple point.
Gives clear ideas with at least one useful reason or example, but development is not consistently detailed or thoughtful.
Gives a basic idea with limited explanation, examples, or reasoning. The answer may be understandable but remains surface-level.
Very brief answer with little elaboration, repeated wording, unclear reasoning, or no supporting example.
No developed idea.

criteria.name: Spoken Language Use
criteria.description: Stimulus-based conversation: assesses grammar, sentence control, vocabulary, clarity, and suitability of spoken English for a Primary 6 oral response. Score strictly: frequent grammar errors, incomplete sentences, unclear references, or very limited vocabulary should reduce the mark even if the main idea can be guessed.

rubric_levels.description: Uses accurate and varied sentence structures with suitable vocabulary. Meaning is clear, natural, and easy to follow throughout.
Uses mostly accurate language with appropriate vocabulary. Errors are noticeable but minor and do not usually affect meaning.
Uses simple but understandable language. Noticeable grammar, sentence control, or word choice errors are present and occasionally affect clarity.
Frequent language errors, limited vocabulary, unclear references, or incomplete sentences affect clarity.
Very limited spoken language evidence, mostly fragmentary language, or response too short to judge securely.
No usable spoken response.

criteria.name: Interaction and Confidence
criteria.description: Stimulus-based conversation: assesses confidence, willingness to continue, responsiveness to prompts, and ability to build on a guiding question if one is given. Score strictly: very short, dependent, or hesitant answers should not receive full credit.

rubric_levels.description: Responds confidently, stays engaged, and builds naturally on the question or guiding prompt with minimal support.
Responds adequately with some confidence, though support, prompting, or extra thinking time may be needed.
Gives a hesitant, very brief, one-word, or dependent response that needs substantial support.
No meaningful interaction or response.
